newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian industrialists see need for 97 mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Italian industrialists see need for 97 mini-budget.

text.p: Italy's industrialist group Confindustria on Monday told a delegation from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) that it believed Italy would need an additional mini-budget next year, it said in a statement.

The statement said measures contained in the government's 1997 budget "were not sufficient to reach the objective of a three-percent ratio between the deficit and GDP and therefore, an additional budget will be necessary in the coming months."
Countries that want to be among founding members of the planned single European currency from 1999 need to reach the three percent deficit/GDP target by next year.

Confindustria said the budget, which parliament must approve by the end of the month, was too heavily weighted in favour of revenue-raising initiatives and was devoid of significant measures aimed at limiting structural spending.
It said Confindustria members told the IMF delegation, which is on a regular visit to Italy, it was worried about consumer price prospects in light of recent higher-than-inflation wage settlements.
"Only a moderate renewal of expiring contracts, consistent with the objects of future inflation, can insure the continuation of the trend of falling inflation," Confindustria said.
